ranked.title: Stop of last resort: confirm the cancel before selling, and never sell on top of a triggered stop
ranked.component: exit tail (a double sale opens a short)
ranked.mechanism: At HEAD 92c404d, enforce_stops accepts legs in status 'Triggered' (src/execution/runner.py:905). It sends cancel_order_id (runner.py:922), which returns True once the cancel is sent rather than confirmed (src/execution/ibkr_trader.py:641-651). In the same pass it sends exit_market (runner.py:926) or exit_limit (runner.py:929). If the in-flight stop fills, the position is sold twice and ends up short. The fix copies the manual ah-exit pattern (scripts/exercise.py:575-590): poll the leg up to 6 x 0.5 s and sell only on Cancelled, ApiCancelled or Inactive. On Filled, close the row on the stop fill. While the leg is still working, send nothing and re-check on the next loop. Sell qty minus whatever the stop already filled, reusing exit_filled_qty from 1d02068. Alert the operator if the cancel is never acknowledged. Same pass, as cleanup only: replace the fixed 0.10 default in exit_limit and flatten_all (ibkr_trader.py:336, 720) with A16's exit_offset. That saves about 0, because the offset caps the price rather than setting it. This item is a prerequisite for M3, M6 and M7.
ranked.expected_saving_R: Mean per trade UNKNOWN; this removes a tail. The 15-s rule has fired once on record (BIYA 09-30, research/paper-exercise/reports/2026-10-01-rules-audit.md:132). On the tape, 10 of 1,867 stop/trail exits had not traded back up to an A16-offset limit by +17.5 s, the delay used for the enforce fallback (props_out.txt:17). That is the order of magnitude of fast falls in which the race can occur. Per incident, the cost is a short of the full quantity bought back across the spread, plus two more orders at a $1 minimum each, i.e. at least $2 = 0.050 R at $40 risk.

ranked.title: Pre-market: probe a server-side SELL STP LMT with outsideRth, and if it works use it only as an outage backstop BELOW the runner's level
ranked.mechanism: The repo's 'queued' probe tested only a plain StopOrder leg (ibkr_trader.py:430), which IBKR documents as RTH-only. IBKR documents STP LMT with Allow Outside RTH as active pre-market, and that has never been probed. If the probe passes, rest one SELL STP LMT per monitored position, with outsideRth, triggerMethod 2 (M4) and limit = stop - exit_offset. Its stop sits below the runner's monitored level by a margin preregistered before any run, and it trails by modify on the same id. The runner stays the primary exit (bid <= level, 5-s loop). When it fires, it modifies that one order (lmtPrice to bid - offset, auxPrice up so it triggers at once) rather than sending a second sell. Do NOT rest it at the level as the primary stop. The cadence study's 'every print' pre-market column, which is what a broker stop at the level amounts to, is the worst cell: -0.523 against -0.379 live. Part of that gap comes from the trail ratcheting on every print, so the comparison is directional.

Latency today costs nothing on average: pre-market drift at D=4 s with flags removed is -0.015 R per exit (props_out.txt:8), with positive-part mean +0.1047 and p99 +0.838 R (props2_out.txt:10). ranked.title: 09:30 handoff: keep a pre-market position watched until its regular-hours stop is actually live
ranked.mechanism: On the first loop at or after 09:30, reprotect gives each monitored row a place_stop (src/execution/runner.py:960-976). That is a StopOrder with no outsideRth (ibkr_trader.py:668-683). set_new_stop_leg then sets protected=1 (src/journal/ledger.py:1229-1234), which drops the row from open_monitored, since that requires protected=0 (ledger.py:998-1000). IBKR's STP and MKT orders are active only after the primary exchange's opening print (KB 35803691), so the position briefly has an inactive stop and no runner watch. enforce_stops' regular-hours action is also a MKT, also inactive until that print. Fix: keep watch_stops on the row until the broker reports the leg working, or until the opening print or 09:31. If the watch fires in that window, act through M1's pattern on the single leg, and have enforce use the limit path until the print. If M6's probe passes, the STP LMT backstop carries across 09:30 and closes the gap.
ranked.expected_saving_R: About 0 R on average; this is a tail guard. On the tape, 32 of 760 stage-1 pre-market fills were still held at 09:30:00. Of those, 18 exited in the 09:30 minute, with gross mean +0.127 R, median -0.110 and worst -1.002 (risk/open_cross_out.txt). There was no blow-up in 2024-26. verdicts.corrected_test_spec:
Book no mean R for M1. It is a safety prerequisite whose tail cannot be measured on the tape at HEAD. Change src/execution only, plus the ah-exit fix in scripts/exercise.py.

A. Design under test:
- enforce_stops becomes two-pass. In loop N it sends the cancel and records cancel_sent_at. In loop N+1 and later it reads the leg.
- SELL only when all three hold: (i) the broker confirmed the cancel, by error 202 for that order id through the existing PaperTrader.order_errors hook (ibkr_trader.py:190-193), or by a server orderStatus Cancelled/ApiCancelled logged after cancel_sent_at, not a status ib_async wrote locally; (ii) the leg's filled count is known; (iii) the qty to sell = held qty minus the leg's filled qty, and is greater than 0.
- On error 10148 or 161 ('cannot be cancelled'), or leg status Filled: never sell. Close the row on the leg's fill.
- On Inactive, PendingCancel, or a working status: no sell. Emit CANCEL UNACKED every loop and block new entries. After K loops (pre-set, e.g. 6 = 30 s), print the human path.
- Add to reconcile_positions: any broker position < 0 prints SHORT, blocks entries and is added to unreconciled.
- Fix ah-exit the same way: no sell when cancel_order_id returns False, or when the leg is Filled or None.

B. Deterministic unit tests (fake trader exposing cancel ack, leg status, leg filled and server-vs-local origin). Each must FAIL at HEAD 92c404d and pass after:
(1) leg already Filled, so cancel returns False: zero shares sold, row closed at the stop fill. HEAD sells qty; reproduced in scratch: 166.
(2) leg Triggered, cancel sent, no ack: no sell for K loops, CANCEL UNACKED printed every loop, entries blocked.
(3) server Cancelled with filled 0: sells qty on the next loop, exactly once.
(4) server Cancelled with filled f, 0<f<qty: sells qty-f.
(5) the leg fills during the ack window: no sell, row closed.
(6) local-only Cancelled (status was Inactive): no sell.
(7) transient Cancelled then PreSubmitted (runner.py:980-982): no sell.
(8) broker position -qty: reconcile prints SHORT. HEAD prints nothing; reproduced in scratch.
(9) ah-exit, same cases (1) and (5).
Rewrite tests/test_runner.py:636-669 to the two-pass behaviour. Then run python3 scripts/test_guards.py and the order-path guard tests; both stay green.

C. Property test: 10,000 runs, cancel latency L ~ U(0,3 s), leg fill instant F ~ U(0,3 s), optional partial fill, loop phase ~ U(0,5 s). Invariant: shares sold by the leg plus by the runner never exceed held qty (zero shorts).
Liveness:
- when the cancel is confirmed with nothing filled, the sale goes out within one loop of the ack in 100% of runs;
- when the ack never comes, an alert appears in 100% of runs.
Report HEAD's short rate on the same draws as the baseline; the scratch run gave 82 of 200.

D. Tape, information only, no look-ahead (A16 offset from spread_out at the exit instant; enforce at t_out+15 s plus loop phase 0/2.5/5 s; fill only on prints after the limit rests). For M3 (STP LMT), count enforce firings and in-window races on exact prints. The scratch result was 5 of 1,867 firings and 0 to 1 races (m1/race.py). This is the exposure M1 must cover before M3 ships. At HEAD (STP market) the tape count is 0 by construction.

E. Live paper, every firing: log the leg status history (trade.log with source), the error codes, bid/ask/last, the ack delay and the sale delay; check broker positions every loop.
Pass:
- zero negative broker positions over all sessions;
- median added exit delay of at most one 5-s loop;
- every unacknowledged cancel alerted.
Fail-closed: any negative position halts entries until a human clears it.

problems: The headline claim is that Fixed beats Tiered by +0.016 R a trade, with high confidence. That figure charges every execution the highest take fee, 0.0030/sh. My recomputation reproduces the arithmetic exactly (Fixed 0.0777 R against Tiered 0.0939 R, n 1873; pre-market +0.0173; m2/m2_out.txt:5-6). The sign, though, depends on an average take fee nobody has measured. At $40 risk the break-even is 0.00183 $/sh (m2_out.txt:28). At 0.0020 Fixed wins by only +0.0023 R; at 0.0013 Tiered wins by 0.0074 R; at 0.0010 Tiered is cheaper on every trade (m2_out.txt:8-10). IBKR's own venue pages show takes cheaper than 0.0030: BYX pays the taker a (0.0002) rebate (web/BYXstkfee.body.txt), IEX non-displayed charges 0.0010 (web/IEXstkfee.body.txt), and IBKRATS passes liquidity-provider rebates through (web/ibkrats_fee.body.txt). So 0.0030 is an upper bound, not a measurement, and 'high' confidence is not supported.

The result depends on position size. At the owner's earlier $20 risk, Tiered all-in is cheaper even at the full 0.0030 take: -0.0097 R a trade, break-even take 0.0037 $/sh, which is above every lit take fee in the copies (m2_out.txt:18, 29). The repo's own holdout already shows this. research/edge-hunt/REPORT.md:66 reports Tiered at +0.132 against the Fixed primary at +0.106 (line 60). That is $20 risk, from scripts/edge_hunt/costs.py:5-14, which already models Fixed against Tiered with take 0.0030 and NSCC 0.0002 and says 'tiered is NOT always cheaper'. The proposal does not cite this earlier work. At $40 risk, 41.2% of trades are under 200 shares (m2_out.txt:4).

The proposal says 'paper commission reports and the model disagree today' as a fact. It is not verified. KB 51685899 gives Tiered only as the DEFAULT for new paper accounts, and the proposal itself says the plan is UNCONFIRMED. Nothing in the repo reads IBKR commissions either: no commissionReport or CommissionReport appears anywhere in src/ or scripts/. The live calibration compares fill prices only. So even a real mismatch changes no repo measurement. Its value is limited to what the owner sees in TWS.

The test spec cannot decide the plan question. KB 60341604 says that on paper 'the broker simulates the role of the exchange' and 'trades are not executed in real markets'. Paper commissions therefore cannot reveal the real venue mix and take fees, which are the one parameter that sets the sign. The spec can only show which plan the paper account is billed on.

The test spec has mechanical gaps. (1) IBKR reports commissions per execution, so the spec must aggregate by order (permId). (2) A modified order counts as a new order for minimums (web/comm_stocks.txt:839). chase_exits re-prices on the same order id (src/execution/runner.py:792-822), so an order can carry two minimums. That hurts Fixed more ($1.00 floor against $0.35 for Tiered): +0.025 R per extra minimum at $40 risk (m2_out.txt:13). (3) Fixed sells also carry the SEC fee (0.0000206 x value, about $0.041 on a $2,000 sale) plus CAT. Left out, they use up most of the $0.05 tolerance. (4) The repo has no code that captures CommissionReport, so a read-only logger is a prerequisite.

'Every leg removes liquidity' is mostly true but not always. A triggered RTH stop-limit, or a pre-market cap limit, whose ask is above the cap rests and adds liquidity. On Tiered, those fills earn rebates.
There is no real-money saving in a paper-only repo, and the proposal says so ('0 R against the backtest model'). The claimed '+0.016 R' would only apply to a live account the project does not trade.
verdicts.corrected_test_spec: This is a bookkeeping check, not a cost saving: 0 R for the paper bot. Do not modify the repo; the logger is a separate read-only script. (1) Capture, read-only: for every paper execution, log execId, permId, side, shares, price, Execution.exchange, time, and the matching CommissionReport (commission, realizedPNL) from ib_async (ib.fills() / commissionReportEvent). Write it to a scratch file, not the ledger. (2) Aggregate by permId. Count a modified order as a new order for minimums (comm_stocks.txt:839), so split at each reprice_exit modification. (3) Pre-register two models before looking at the data. Fixed: min(max(1, 0.005q), max(1, 0.01 q px)), plus 0.0000206 x value on sells, plus 0.000003 x q. Tiered: min(max(0.35, 0.0035q), max(0.35, 0.01 q px)), plus the take or add fee for the venue in Execution.exchange from the IBKR venue pages, plus min(0.0002q, 0.005 q px), plus commission x (0.000175 + 0.00056), plus the same regulatory fees. (4) Use at least 20 orders, with at least 5 under 100 shares and at least 5 of 200 shares or more; those are the size bands where the $1.00 and $0.35 floors separate the plans. The account is on whichever model lands within $0.03 of the reported commission on at least 90% of orders. If neither does, report 'unclassified' and do not guess. (5) If the account is Tiered: either file the paper ticket (KB 51685899, effective the next business day per KB 35797944) or reconcile paper P&L with the Tiered model, and declare that it is a paper simulation. ## 15. What this could mean for the bot (hypotheses, not measurements)

1. **RTH entry.** The bot's buy stop-limit, capped at trigger + max(1¢, 0.3%), works out to 1–3¢ over the trigger for $2–$10 names. That's far tighter than his 5–20¢, and it's the order type his ZfwTJAMLroA stream says "probably wouldn't have gotten filled". The corpus equivalent is the pre-market runner's design: a limit at the ask plus an offset once the ask reaches the trigger.
2. **Exit offsets.** The bot's A16 rule, max(1% of bid, spread) clamped to 3–10¢, is inside his 5–15¢ practice. It also respects his warnings about rejects and market makers on cheap names.
3. **Pre-market.** The runner's design (extended-hours limit with an offset, no resting stop, monitored bail at bid minus offset) matches the corpus on every point.
4. **Testable on the local tick data.** Two candidates: the offset size and the entry style (stop-limit versus ask-plus-offset).

## Verdict

The doctrine is consistent: limit orders only, priced through the market by a fixed cents offset (about 10¢), entered at or a few cents before the break when the tape turns green. Profits are sold on the ask and losses bailed through the bid; stops are mental. Bigger spreads mean smaller size or a pass.

There are only two numeric spread anchors: a maximum of 15–20¢ under $10, and a stop about one spread below the bid. Everything in section 14 is absent.
